summary: Jun Yang works in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang held posts as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a research fellow (受託研究員) at Koyasan University.

Jundo Nagashima is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, also studying under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. Nagashima was a researcher and lecturer at Taisho University.

June McDaniel is a religious studies scholar and Indologist. She earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD from the University of Chicago (1980-1986), becoming Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston in 1988.

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Dongguk University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, Seung-suk Jung, and Sungdoo Ahn, Bang has served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Ha earned an MA at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe, later serving as Professor at Keimyung University.

Buddhist scholar and Indologist Junjirō Takakusu (1866-1945) studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Max Müller, Winternitz, and Sylvain Lévi. He was Professor (1897-1927) and President (1930-1945) of the University of Tokyo.

Junkei Washio (1868-1941) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1888-1893). He held professorships at Toyo University (~1904-1926) and Komazawa University (~1926-1935), also teaching at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (b. 1935), a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as associate professor at Hokkaido University and held director and chancellor positions at IIBS and ICPBS.

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received an MA from the Australian National University in 1980, completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen in 1990, and became a professor at IIBS.

Junko Minamoto (b. 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed graduate courses at Ryukoku University (1972-1975) and Otani University (1975-1980), and served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang (1886-1969) worked in philosophy and Sinology. He studied under Liang Qichao, attended Waseda University (~1906-1910) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913-1915), and held posts at Peking University (~1918-1920) and Tsinghua University (~1920-1922).

Junsho Kato (b. 1934) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at KU Leuven and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1986), he held professorships at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University, and an appointment at Reitaku University.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888-1968) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. Educated at Kansai University, he later held academic posts at Ryukoku University (~1920-1948) and Kansai University (~1924-1960).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section chief (課長) at Otani University.

Juri Lotman (1922-1993) was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University between 1939 and 1961, and held a post at the University of Tartu beginning in 1954.

Jurij Andreevič Smirnov (1923-1984) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1948-1954) and served as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1967.

Shigeaki Watanabe is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. Watanabe held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989-1990) and Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies as Professor (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Justin Edwards Abbott (1853-1932) was a scholar in Indology who completed an A.B. at Dartmouth College (~1872-1876) and studied at Union Theological Seminary (~1876-1879).

Justin Hartley Moore (1884-1962), a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Columbia University (1908) under A. V. Williams Jackson and David P. Jackson. He taught French and Romanic languages at City College of New York.
